businessVision: ProjectOS delivers ordinary technical work on real projects end to end: Claude implements, the ChatGPT gatekeeper reviews through the trusted broker without the owner's relay, and ProjectOS carries each approved phase through checks, review, commit, push and closure; where the owner has delegated the closure commit to ProjectOS, a phase closes with no owner act at all, and the owner holds every protected action.
definitionOfComplete: Nine phases are complete: the temporary pieces created for the live proofs are retired and spending is disabled once the key is revoked (PROJECTOS-COMPLETION1A); and before it: one `projectos continue` carries a phase from work to closed, a phase that changes its own required validator is judged by that new copy as well as the base copy, and a third agency phase proves both with no owner act; and before them: phase write grants come from a structured list of paths in the approved plan, with the judging validators run from the last approved commit; phase closure works for any governed project; the ChatGPT gatekeeper answers without the owner's relay through the trusted broker (owner decision of 2026-10-25); ProjectOS has carried one ordinary phase end to end on a new governed project, the website of an SEO and social-media posting agency, with evidence; a project whose owner grants the closure-decision-commit scope has its delegate's closure decision committed by ProjectOS itself, with a model-invented decision time refused; and a second agency phase has closed end to end with no owner act. Dead Aisle and PolyGo are not part of this plan (owner decision of 2026-10-25). Host-attested unattended review, the signed installer, Forge and the Control Center redesign are deferred and are reopened only by an owner decision.

Running a phase's required validators and the loop's enforcement code from the last approved commit, so work under review cannot alter what judges it.
Generalising the closure eligibility gate from the project id 'projectos' to the governed project's own id.

Folding the run's own records into the loop's technical-continuation commit, and committing generated closure-tail records as a technical action when the phase's owner gates leave commit and push delegated.

Live proofs: the disposable two-phase proof re-run with the reduced owner acts, then one ordinary phase on a new local governed project — the website of an SEO and social-media posting agency — through projectos continue, with evidence under docs/finish/.

phases.description: The EXIT-PROOF1A precondition probe (2026-10-29, live Codex CLI 0.165.0 on this host) showed: with --ignore-user-config and no Windows sandbox mode Codex can run no command at all (every read "rejected: blocked by policy"), so the reviewer could never review; with windows.sandbox set (elevated or unelevated) reads work and writes inside and outside the checkout are blocked ("Access to the path ... is denied"); Codex reports every command wrapped in an absolute powershell.exe -Command, which the out-of-checkout heuristic reads as a path outside the repository, refusing every review; both sandbox modes can still read the owner profile (the residual the owner accepted as tripwire-only: "Accept tripwires (Recommended)"). This phase makes the adapter set the Windows sandbox mode itself (fixed, not configurable) and analyse the command inside a known shell wrapper.
phases.scope: Edit the Codex adapter, its tests and its validator rules only.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows the adapter always passes a fixed Windows sandbox mode; a configured argument cannot change or remove it; tested.

A command reported inside a known shell wrapper (absolute powershell.exe/pwsh.exe -Command, cmd.exe /c, bash -lc) is judged by its inner command; an unknown wrapper or an inner command reaching outside the checkout is still a denial; tested with the exact forms the probe recorded.
Every new rule has a validator pin and a named mutation.

phases.description: Setting up the Stage 1 exit proof, the agency plan v1.4 was refused PLAN_INCOMPLETE because D11 R5 ("every phase needs an independent review") was applied to the agency's three phases that CLOSED before D11 existed. A closed phase is history: no review can now be added to it, and refusing every later plan for it leaves a pre-D11 project unable to plan at all. R5 is now skipped for a phase only when it is already in the ACTIVE approved plan AND its COMMITTED phase record says closed; a new or open phase still needs an independent review. Owner: "Fix ProjectOS properly (Recommended)", 2026-10-30, approving the change to the protected planApproval.ts.
phases.scope: Edit planApproval.ts and the role-review validator; add tests.
acceptanceCriteria: A plan whose only self-review-only phases are closed (committed record) and already in the active plan is approved; the same phase not closed, closed only in the working tree, or absent from the active plan is refused; tested.
The role-review validator pins the exemption to exactly those two conditions with named mutations.

phases.description: The exit proof's first run (2026-10-30 09:30, agency SEO-AGENCY-SITE-CHECK3A) had its Codex review refused as "attempted tools it was denied". A traced re-run of the same adapter path against the same candidate showed the only denial was a false positive: the reviewer piped a Node probe script into node, and the script's JavaScript string "\\nExpires: ..." (a quote followed by an escaped newline) matched the UNC tripwire as the network path \\nExpires. Nothing left the checkout. A denial ends the run on the owner, so this false positive alone defeats the zero-owner-act exit proof. This phase makes the UNC tripwire require a host followed by a separator (\\host\share, //host/share, \\?\UNC\..., \\.\pipe\...), which every path into a share has, and which a quoted escape does not. The exit proof runs after it.
phases.scope: Edit the Codex adapter, its tests and its validator rules only.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact command the exit proof's reviewer ran is not a denial; \\host\share, //host/share, \\?\UNC\host\share and \\.\pipe\name paths still are; tested.
The UNC rule has a validator pin and a named mutation that is killed.

phases.description: The exit proof's second run (2026-10-30 10:56) had its Codex review refused again as "attempted tools it was denied", with no record of which tripwire fired. Five traced reviews of the same candidate showed why: Codex writes and runs Node scripts that execute the candidate's own validator, and those scripts trip the text tripwires on innocent content (a JavaScript ".." string read as a parent escape; a failed script whose output carried git's own sandbox warning "unable to access '.../.config/git/ignore': Permission denied"). With one added sentence telling the reviewer to review by reading only (git diff/show/log and file reads; no scripts; run no repository code, the loop already ran it), three of three traced reviews ran no script, tripped nothing, and still found the candidate's real defect. Separately, a reviewer REJECT whose findings are all MEDIUM or LOW reaches the gatekeeper as "returned REJECT" with no finding text, so the gatekeeper cannot name a correction. This phase: (1) adds the read-only reviewing sentence to the review instruction; (2) names the reviewer's denial reasons in the refusal; (3) carries a rejection's findings (bounded, inert) into the stop detail when none is CRITICAL or HIGH; (4) ignores git's own config-access warning line when deciding that a failed Codex command was stopped by the sandbox. The exit proof runs after it.
phases.scope: Edit the review instruction, the independent review refusal and objection texts, the Codex adapter, their tests and validator rules only.
acceptanceCriteria: The review instruction tells the reviewer to review by reading only and to run no script or repository code; tested and pinned.
A review refused for denied tools names the denial reasons, bounded and inert; tested.
A REJECT with only MEDIUM or LOW findings puts those findings (bounded, inert) in the stop detail; a REJECT still credits no review; tested.
A failed Codex command whose only sandbox-shaped output is git's config-access warning is not a denial; any other sandbox wording still is; tested and pinned with a named mutation.

phases.description: The exit proof's third run (2026-10-30 12:40) got a clean cross-provider review for the first time: Codex read the candidate and returned REJECT with two real MEDIUM findings, and the gatekeeper, now shown them, answered AMENDMENT_REQUIRED with a precise instruction. The loop then refused the correction: "the amendment named no path to correct". ProjectOS grants a correction worker only the files the amendment instruction names (pathsNamedIn, inside the phase's approved maximum), but nothing tells the gatekeeper so: its evidence pack says only "Edit(path) and Write(path) only", which it copied as the literal allowedActions "Edit(path)"; and the reviewer cited "validate-site.cjs:195" without its folder. This phase tells the gatekeeper, in the correctionMechanism part of its evidence, to name each file to correct by its full repository-relative path from workerWritableMaximum, and asks the reviewer to cite files by their repository-relative path. The correction boundary itself (protected) is unchanged: an amendment that names no permitted path is still refused. The exit proof runs after it. The ECC SECURITY review of this phase then showed a deeper gap: the production run command never supplies a correction maximum (always empty), and by design a correction maximum may not include the phase's own implementation files, so an independent reviewer's REJECT had no fix route at all and every rejection ended on the owner. Owner, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "Claude fixes, re-review (Recommended)" — on an independent rejection, the loop re-runs the same implementer with the reviewer's findings, writing only the files the plan already approved for the phase, up to the existing limit of three corrections, then re-runs the checks and obtains a fresh independent review. No new permission: the grant is the phase's own approved writePaths, re-issued for that one dispatch only; a rejection still never counts as a pass; when the budget is spent the run stops as before. The ECC SECURITY recheck accepted the route as an owner-authorised narrowing but required the protected rule BC-8n (val-projectos-boot-continue1a.cjs: "a correction dispatch never carries the implementer's write grant") to be reworded honestly before closure. Owner, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "Yes, reword it (Recommended)" — BC-8n states that a correction never carries the implementer's write grant EXCEPT the one dispatch right after an independent reviewer's rejection, limited to the phase's approved files and the existing three-attempt budget, as rule RC-1 checks; its check still fails if the grant reaches any other dispatch.
phases.scope: Edit the loop runner, the review instruction, the Claude adapter's correction instruction, their tests and validator rules only.
acceptanceCriteria: The gatekeeper's evidence tells it to name every file to correct by its full repository-relative path, taken from workerWritableMaximum, with an example from that list, and that an amendment naming none is refused before any worker starts; it no longer offers the placeholder text Edit(path); tested and pinned.
The review instruction asks the reviewer to cite each file by its repository-relative path; tested and pinned.
An amendment instruction that names a permitted file by that path is authorised, and one that names none is still refused; tested.

An independent REJECT (or a CRITICAL/HIGH finding) with correction budget left re-dispatches the implementer with the phase's approved write grant and an instruction pointing at the reviewer record, counts one correction, re-runs the checks and obtains a fresh independent review; tested.

A rejection never credits the review; when the budget is spent the run stops REVIEW_OUTSTANDING as before; a gatekeeper-directed correction still never receives the approved write grant; tested and pinned.
When the correction maximum is empty, the gatekeeper is told that no file is correctable by it rather than pointed at an empty list; the reviewer prompt quotes its example path; tested.
BC-8n states the one owner-approved exception and refers to RC-1; it still fires if the approved grant reaches any dispatch other than the one after a rejection; its named mutations are killed.

phases.description: V4 Stage 2, per docs/changes/delta_spec.md revision 2, approved by the owner in Plan Mode on 2026-11-01. No envelope exists in code today, so this phase builds it. ADR-T1 states the principal (the Windows operator plus the project the work is bound to; a Supabase identity carries no kernel authority), tenant versus domain, the registry trust basis, the linked-worktree rule, credential classes, and what Stage 2 does not prove. Owner decisions: "Accept it (Recommended)" for ADR-K1; "Agency apart, rest mine (Recommended)" for the tenant split, with PolyGo listed as the second owner-personal project and its repository untouched.
phases.scope: Write ADR-T1; mark ADR-K1 Accepted on the owner's word; add the committed tenant and action registries; add pure core code for tenant, the envelope v2 rules R1 to R5 and the action registry; sync stale docs.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-T1 states every limit in the delta section "What Stage 2 does not prove", including that a worker can reach any tenant's secrets and files outside the kernel, and the owner's hard rule that no other party's data or credentials go on this machine until Stage 4 isolation and service-held secrets are done.
The registry binds projectId, repository and governedRoot to a tenant and a domain; a duplicate or wildcard refuses the whole file, tested.
The action registry names both existing vocabularies, and cross-tenant-access and tenant-registry-change are P5; an unregistered action is P5, tested.
A missing or unparseable envelope field is refused (R1); a child that changes tenant, domain, project or environment is refused (R3), tested.
Validator pin and named mutations, each killed by its own rule.

phases.description: Replace the using(true) policies with tenant-bound access, as forward-only transactional migrations, and prove them on a throwaway local cluster shaped like Supabase. Live facts on 2026-11-01: sign-up was open, and any signed-in account could rewrite every row, so existing rows may be stranger-written. Nothing in the product reads these tables. This phase touches no production system; the live apply is a separate owner act using the exact bytes proved here, after a passed read-only preflight (owner: "Connect the plugin (Recommended)").
phases.scope: Add baseline and tenant-boundary migrations, a read-only live preflight, a harness with an auth stub, a non-superuser migration owner and the ported privilege gate; retire schema.sql and interactive.sql; remove the dead fetchProjects and its silent seed fallback; correct the false comments.
acceptanceCriteria: Table grants are the first wall: nothing for anon, no TRUNCATE for any client role, and no client update of tenant_id, id or project_id.
With both tenants seeded, a member sees their own rows (positive control) and none of the other tenant's, in all four tables.
Every cross-tenant write is refused, including by a user who owns both tenants, and nobody can add themselves to tenant_members.
anon, an authenticated non-member and null-claims authenticated read nothing.

The ported privilege gate, judged on effective privileges, reports nothing, and these mutations each fail the harness: using(true); auth.uid() is not null; a to public policy; USAGE on private granted to anon; an added public function.
Backfill comes from an explicit project-to-tenant map, raises on any unmapped row, and the column has no default; the migration ends with an in-transaction check; both apply twice on a fresh cluster.
A re-run of the retired SQL files cannot recreate a permissive policy, tested.

Owner decision, 2026-11-01, "Yes, lock by default (Recommended)": a new table, sequence or function made by postgres in public gives anon and authenticated nothing, tested with a positive control, and existing objects keep their grants.

phases.description: Tenant comes from the committed installation registry for the project the work is bound to, never from worker text, arguments or environment. It is recorded at admission, and a refusal that cannot be recorded stops the operation, because appendRefusal in mcp/bridge.ts drops silently today. Changing the registry is a P5 action: the owner must have made its last commit. Authorship stays a git name until signed commits exist.
phases.scope: Add the committed-bytes registry reader with whole-file validation and the owner-last-commit check; derive tenant in the governed context; mint and record envelopes at the crossing points; add TENANT_UNKNOWN and TENANT_MISMATCH and a read-only tenant show.

A refusal that cannot be recorded stops the operation, tested.
With the project check disabled by mutation, a bridge read across tenants is still refused by the tenant rule.
Linked worktrees follow the ADR-T1 rule, and governed runs still work in one, tested.
Validator pin and named mutations, each killed by its own rule.

phases.description: The operation path has no real project check today: operation-gate.cjs passes projectId: ref.project, so the vault compares a reference with itself. Each credential declares its reach, so an account-wide token is never projected into another tenant's session. The stored format is unchanged and no secret is re-entered.

A tenant secret is released to a second project in the same tenant (positive control) and refused across tenants; only the tenant rule can decide this.
A project id starting with tenant., in any case, is refused, and provision, remove and present are bound, tested with synthetic entries.
The platform credential is released to no tenant session, tested.

An operation release needs a committed grant naming the project, the exact references, the action and an expiry; a record for another phase, project, credential or a stale date releases nothing, tested. Found by review 2026-11-02.
An account-wide token is not projected into another tenant's session, tested.
Validator pin and named mutations, each killed by its own rule.

phases.description: The Control Center has no CSP (csp: null). A wrong policy can blank the app, so this is proved in a real app window and not only by reading config. The installed app gets it only when the MSI is next rebuilt.

Validator pin and named mutations, each killed by its own rule.

phases.description: Owner decision, 2026-11-01: "Rules now, connectors later (Recommended)". This phase writes what every connector must declare (tenant, scopes, secret reference, data categories, idempotency, last acceptance date), the release gate that blocks an unqualified connector, and the standard execution receipt and error vocabulary, including outcome_unknown. The acceptance scenarios from the blueprint are defined here; cross-tenant denial is proved in Stage 2 and the other eight first run in Stage 5. Task ledger and webhooks stay in Stage 4 and 5; channel adapters stay in Stage 5 onward in the owner's agreed order.

Validator pin and named mutations, each killed by its own rule.

phases.description: Prove on three real projects that the database and the kernel's own routes each refuse a cross-tenant read: projectos and polygo in owner-personal, seo-agency in agency-business. The same-tenant pair is what lets the proof fail. A proof counts only if removing its rule makes it fail. Spend is $0, so no temporary allowlist entry is needed. The owner's live database apply, with a passed preflight, comes before this phase. This is not a boundary against a hostile worker, and the evidence says so.

Live and read-only, after the owner's apply: sign-up disabled, no permissive policy on any public table, tables out of realtime, anon reads nothing.

phases.description: First phase of docs/changes/delta_spec_V4_PORTS.md, approved by the owner on 2026-11-01 ("Approved"). Owner's rule: "i want to claim it's mine with giving credits to the due".
